horizon-definitions.SafeFor: For a natural number p, an angel strategy A, a devil strategy D, and a natural number n, SafeFor(p,A,D,n) means that for every natural number m with m < n, the displacement from the current point at time m to the current point at time m+1 has each coordinate between −p and p, inclusive, and the optional value containing that destination does not occur in the burned list at time m+1. Play starts with visited list [(0,0)] and empty burned list; in each round D receives the visited list and appends either a point or no point to the burned list, then A receives the visited list and this updated burned list and appends its chosen point to the visited list. Current means the last visited point, defaulting to (0,0) on an empty list. The condition for n=0 is vacuous; zero displacement is allowed.
horizon-definitions.FiniteAngelWins: For natural numbers p and n, FiniteAngelWins(p,n) means that there exists one total angel strategy A, taking a list of integer lattice points and a list of optional integer lattice points to an integer lattice point, such that for every total devil strategy D, taking a list of integer lattice points to an optional integer lattice point, all rounds m < n of their play have displacement in [−p,p] in each coordinate and land at a point whose optional value is absent from the burned list after that round. The strategy A is chosen before D; there are no restrictions on D's outputs or its behavior on any histories. At n=0 no round is checked.
horizon-definitions.Observation: An observation is an arbitrary pair (h,b), where h is a finite list of integer lattice points and b is a finite list of optional integer lattice points. There are no conditions on list lengths, consistency, legality, or reachability.
horizon-definitions.BoundedMove: For a natural number p, a bounded move is a pair of natural numbers (i,j), each strictly less than 2p+1, with these bounds included in its type. Thus each coordinate ranges from 0 through 2p inclusive; when p=0 the only pair is (0,0).
horizon-definitions.decodeMove: For a natural number p, any finite list h of integer lattice points, and a bounded move (i,j) with 0 ≤ i,j < 2p+1, decodeMove returns (u₁+i−p,u₂+j−p), with arithmetic in the integers, where u is h's last point or (0,0) when h is empty. No legality or reachability condition is imposed on h.
horizon-definitions.boundedAngel: For a natural number p and any total function f from observations to pairs of natural numbers less than 2p+1, boundedAngel(p,f) is the total angel strategy which, on any lists h and b, evaluates f(h,b)=(i,j) and returns (u₁+i−p,u₂+j−p), where u is the last point of h or (0,0) if h is empty. This formula applies also to observations that never occur in play and does not inspect whether the destination is burned.
horizon-definitions.encodeAngel: For a natural number p and any total angel strategy A, encodeAngel(p,A) is a noncomputable function on all observations (h,b). Set v=A(h,b) and let u be the last point of h, defaulting to (0,0). If each coordinate of v−u lies in [−p,p], return the bounded pair whose coordinates are the natural-number conversions of v₁−u₁+p and v₂−u₂+p. Integer-to-natural conversion truncates negative integers to zero, although the stated branch condition makes these two expressions nonnegative. Otherwise return (p,p). Both coordinates of the result are strictly less than 2p+1. The same rule applies to arbitrary off-play histories and to empty h; a burned destination does not affect the branch choice.

game-definitions.advance: For any state s, optional integer lattice point d, and integer lattice point v, advance(s,d,v) is the state with visited list s.visited followed by v and burned list s.burned followed by d. This construction imposes no legality, length, or consistency requirements.
game-definitions.Viable: For a natural number p, Viable(p,0,s) is true for every state s. For a natural number n, Viable(p,n+1,s) means that for every optional integer lattice point d there exists an integer lattice point v such that each coordinate of v−current(s) lies in [−p,p], the optional value containing v is absent from s.burned followed by d, and Viable(p,n,advance(s,d,v)) holds. Here current(s) is the last visited point, or (0,0) for an empty visited list, and advance appends v and d to the respective lists. The existential v may depend on d; this alternating quantifier pattern is repeated at each remaining round. Every state and every optional d is included, without reachability restrictions; d may be absent, repeated, or any point.
game-definitions.finiteAngel: For natural numbers p and T, finiteAngel(p,T) is a noncomputable total angel strategy. On any lists h and b, if there exists an integer lattice point v whose displacement from the last point of h (or (0,0) for empty h) lies in [−p,p] in each coordinate, whose optional value is absent from b, and for which Viable(p,T−length(h),(h followed by v,b)) holds, it returns an unspecified classically chosen witness v of this entire conjunction. Otherwise it returns (0,0). Subtraction is natural-number subtraction, truncated at zero, so when length(h) ≥ T the viability condition has horizon zero and is true. The rule includes empty and inconsistent lists and all off-play observations; in the fallback case no legality or safety property of (0,0) is required.
game-definitions.badMove: For natural numbers p and n and any state s, badMove(p,n,s) is a noncomputable optional integer lattice point. If there exists an optional point d such that for every integer lattice point v, displacement in [−p,p] in each coordinate from current(s) to v and absence of the optional value containing v from s.burned followed by d imply that Viable(p,n,advance(s,d,v)) is false, it returns an unspecified classically chosen such d. Otherwise it returns no point. Current defaults to (0,0) for an empty visited list; advance appends v and d. The quantified implication holds vacuously for illegal or burned destinations, and the universal condition is vacuous if there is no legal unburned destination. No reachability condition is imposed on s, and the chosen d may itself be no point.
game-definitions.simulatedBurns: For any total function choose from states to optional integer lattice points and any finite point list h, simulatedBurns(choose,h) is defined recursively on h's length. It returns the empty list when h is empty. Otherwise set prior to h with its last entry removed; if prior is empty, again return the empty list. If prior is nonempty, first set b=simulatedBurns(choose,prior), then return b followed by choose(prior,b). Thus empty and singleton histories both yield an empty burned list; longer histories reconstruct one optional output for each nonempty proper prefix in increasing prefix length. The input history need not start at the origin or satisfy any movement condition.
game-definitions.historyDevil: For any total function choose from states to optional integer lattice points, historyDevil(choose) is the total devil strategy which, on an arbitrary point history h, returns choose applied to the state with visited list h and burned list simulatedBurns(choose,h). The latter list is empty for histories of length zero or one and otherwise recursively appends choose's output on each nonempty proper prefix together with the outputs already reconstructed for earlier prefixes. This rule is defined on all histories without legality or reachability assumptions.
game-definitions.finiteDevil: For natural numbers p and T, finiteDevil(p,T) is the noncomputable historyDevil obtained from the state function choose(s)=badMove(p,T−length(s.visited),s), with natural subtraction truncated at zero. On a history h it first reconstructs b by this same choose function on nonempty proper prefixes, then applies badMove(p,T−length(h),(h,b)). For each such badMove call with horizon n, if some optional d makes every legal unburned successor fail Viable(p,n,·), a classically chosen such d is returned; otherwise no point is returned. Legal means coordinate displacement in [−p,p], and unburned means the destination's optional value is absent from the current burned list followed by d. At histories of length at least T the badMove horizon is zero. Empty, singleton, illegal, and all other off-play histories are included in this total definition.

compactness: For every natural number p, assume that for every natural number n there exists an angel strategy Aₙ such that for every devil strategy D all rounds m < n of the resulting play are safe. Then there exists one angel strategy A such that for every devil strategy D and every natural number m the round from time m to m+1 is safe. In both premise and conclusion strategies are total functions: the angel takes a finite point history and a finite list of optional burned points and returns a point, while the devil takes a finite point history and returns an optional point. Play starts at (0,0) with no burned entries; each round first appends the devil's optional output, then appends the angel's destination chosen using that updated burned list. Safety means each coordinate of the displacement is between −p and p inclusive and the optional destination is absent from the burned list after the round. The premise permits the chosen angel strategy to depend on n, but the conclusion chooses a single angel before both D and m. The n=0 premise checks no rounds; p=0 is included; no additional restrictions are imposed on the devil, and no escape or distinct-visit condition is asserted.
finite-determinacy: For every pair of natural numbers p and T, either there exists an angel strategy A such that for every devil strategy D all rounds m < T of their play are safe, or there exists one devil strategy D such that for every angel strategy A it is false that all rounds m < T of their play are safe. The disjunction is inclusive. Strategies are arbitrary total functions: A takes point and optional-burn histories to a point, and D takes a point history to an optional point. Starting from visited list [(0,0)] and empty burned list, each round appends D's output before A selects and appends a destination using the updated burned list. A safe round has both coordinate displacements in [−p,p] and its optional destination absent from the burned list after that round. In the second alternative D is chosen before A; the negation applies to the whole universal safety condition up to T, without specifying a common failing round for all A. Natural numbers p=0 and T=0 are included; at T=0 the universal safety condition is vacuous, so its negation in the second alternative is false for every pair of strategies. Neither alternative imposes any additional restriction on devil choices or requires escape.
